memo_markdown:
*Synthetic data throughout.*

## Last week's moves
- **LinkedIn: $450/day to $0.** Worked. It had 0 conversions on $5,028 over its last two weeks of spend (10-19 and 10-26). Spend is now $0. Account conversions were 325 vs 355 the week before, and no tracked LinkedIn sales were lost (0 conversions in both weeks).
- **Meta: $500 to $400/day.** Worked so far. Spend was $2,764 for the 7 days (vs $3,566 the week before). CPA fell from $105 to $89, and ROAS is 1.97 vs the 1.5 target.

## What's happening
- **Google Search:** CPA $19.64, ROAS 9.86, steady (3-week CPA $18.26 vs $18.13 earlier). Healthy.
- **Meta:** 3-week CPA $97 vs $75 earlier (+30%). That is under the 40% trigger and I have already trimmed it.
- **Email:** CPA $23.58 on 12 conversions, and the 3-week CPA is flat ($18.65 vs $17.48). Spend is tiny ($283).
- **Direct:** 8.9 conversions per day vs 1.5 early on, with paid spend at 0.95x. Self-reported ChatGPT/AI answers were 26% in the latest week (24% "Asked ChatGPT" plus 2% "AI assistant recommended you"), up from 6% early on, on 100 responses. Untracked AI referral is the likely driver, not paid.
- **LinkedIn:** self-reported share is 0% for 3 weeks (was 4-9%).

## Moves
- No budget changes. Google $600, Meta $400, Email $40 and LinkedIn $0 stay as they are. Meta is above target in every model, and cutting further before the holdout is unjustified.

## Where the models disagree
- **Google Search:** share is 39% (first touch) to 68% (last touch). ROAS is 5.7-10.1, well above target in every model.
- **Email:** share is 4% to 22%. ROAS is 9.9-52.5, above target in every model.
- **Meta:** ROAS is 2.7-4.2, above target in every model.
- **LinkedIn:** ROAS is 1.04 (last touch) to 2.19. Four of five models are above 1.5, so I will not cut it for efficiency alone. The pause is for the zero conversions.

## Test to run
- **LinkedIn:** audit tracking since 10-17 first. If it is fixed, relaunch at about $100/day for 3 weeks with a geo holdout.
- **Still open from last week:** the Meta geo holdout (4 weeks) and the direct and AI-assistant tracking test.

## Confidence
Medium. I would change course if:
- the Meta holdout shows incremental ROAS under 1.5, in which case I would cut it;
- LinkedIn tracking turns out to be intact, in which case its zero conversions are real and it stays off;
- direct falls back as AI answers fade, which would mean paid was part of the cause.

*All data in this report is synthetic.*

## Last week's moves
First run, so there are no prior moves to judge.

## What's happening
- **LinkedIn:** 0 conversions from 10-18 to 10-31 on $5,328 spend. Daily spend rose from about $300 to $460. 3-week CPA is $891 vs $144 earlier. Self-reported LinkedIn share is 0% for the last two weeks (4-9% before). It could be a tracking break, but the spend is waste either way.
- **Meta:** 3-week CPA is $96 vs $64 earlier (+50%) on flat spend. The shift began 10-02 ($60 to $100). Last-week ROAS is 1.87 vs the 1.5 target. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from ~19% to ~9%.
- **Google Search:** Stable. CPA is $18.43 and ROAS 10.7. The 9/12-9/18 spend spike (peak week $6,341) held CPA at about $19, so it was fine.
- **Email:** CPA is $16 over the last 3 weeks vs $20 earlier, and ROAS is 9.1. Healthy.
- **Direct:** 1.5 to 8.1 conversions/day (5.4x) with paid spend at 1.05x. Self-reported "AI assistant" plus "Asked ChatGPT" is now ~28% of answers (week of 10-26), up from ~4% in early August. This points to AI-assistant referrals, not paid.

## Moves
- LinkedIn: $450/day to $0. Zero results for 14 days. Check tracking before relaunch.
- Meta: $500/day to $400/day (-20%). CPA is up 50%, but the models put ROAS at 2.7-4.2, so I trimmed it rather than cut it.
- Google Search and Email: no change.

## Where the models disagree
- Google Search credit ranges from 38% (first-touch) to 68% (last-touch). ROAS is 5.7-10.1, above target under every model. No move.
- Email credit ranges from 4% (last-touch) to 23% (first-touch). ROAS is 10-54. Email is probably undervalued by last click, but it is too small to matter much.
- LinkedIn ROAS is 1.04-2.16. It is below target under last-touch only. Models can't settle it, but the zero-conversion rule overrides them.

## Test to run
- Meta geo holdout: suppress Meta in ~20% of matched regions for 4 weeks. Measure total conversions across all channels, including direct.
- Direct: add a tracked "how did you hear about us" field with AI-assistant options and an AI referral UTM. This confirms the AI source before any budget moves.

## Confidence
Medium overall. High on the LinkedIn pause, medium on the Meta trim. I would restore Meta if the holdout shows incremental ROAS above 1.5 and the CPA rise is only attribution drift. I would relaunch LinkedIn if tracking turns out to be broken and CRM data shows conversions.
